learning_outcomes.text: Has basic knowledge of concepts related to electromagnetic compatibility and power quality, electromagnetic disturbances, principles of standardization and measurement assessment of voltage quality.
Has knowledge of the classification of voltage RMS disturbances, slow and rapid voltage changes.
Has knowledge of voltage and current distortion: harmonic and interharmonic in the band up to 2.5 kHz and emission of high-frequency disturbances in converter systems.
Has basic knowledge of the cooperation of power electronic systems with the supply network.
Has basic knowledge of voltage sags and swells and short interruptions in supply.
Has basic knowledge of voltage and current asymmetry.
Has basic knowledge of reactive power compensation and the operation of capacitors in an environment of distorted voltages and currents.
Has basic knowledge of the cooperation of distributed energy sources with the supply network.
Has basic knowledge of uninterruptible power supplies and the costs of poor energy quality.
Can assess the quality of electricity supply based on single-point measurements.
Can analyze and draw conclusions regarding the causes of poor electricity supply quality and propose technical measures to eliminate the effects of poor voltage quality.
Can prepare documentation regarding the implementation of an engineering task and prepare a text discussing the results of this task.
Can work individually and in a team; can estimate the time needed to complete an assigned task; can develop and implement a work schedule to meet deadlines.
Is aware of the responsibility for their own work and is ready to adhere to teamwork principles and take responsibility for jointly implemented tasks.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the issues of electromagnetic compatibility, electromagnetic disturbance classification, basic definitions, standardization, basic assessment of the power quality
Classification of voltage RMS disturbances, slow voltage changes (sources, method of numerical description and measurement principles, effects, voltage stabilization methods); quick voltage changes

Voltage fluctuations - sources, effects, method of numerical description and measurement principles, ways of flicker eliminating, location of flicker sources, propagation of flicker in the power system, summation of voltage fluctuations

Voltage and current distortion - power theories in circuits with distorted waveforms, sources, effects, method of numerical description and measurement principles, methods of elimination, source location, harmonic propagation in the power system, passive and active filtration, interharmonics
Impact of power electronic converters on the power supply network, power electronic interfaces of distributed energy sources and consumers

Voltage dips - sources, effects, method of numerical description and measurement principles, methods of elimination, location of sources, propagation in the power system, DVR system, contract for the power supply

Asymmetry of voltages and currents - sources, effects, method of numerical description and measurement principles, methods of elimination, location of sources, propagation of asymmetry in the power system
Capacitor as an element of the power system - reactive power compensation and filtration systems
High frequency disturbances in power electronics systems
Distributed energy sources and voltage quality
Energy quality and the electricity market
Uninterruptible power supply systems, energy storage

assessment_methods.method: Participation in a discussion during lectures

assessment_rules: For lectures, positive test results and attendance are required. For laboratory classes, attendance, positive test results, and completion of the laboratory are required. Completion of the module is possible after completing all laboratory classes.
